newsitem.title: JORDAN: Newly-listed stocks pull Jordanian bourse down.
newsitem.headline: Newly-listed stocks pull Jordanian bourse down.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange fell 0.26 percent on Tuesday in quiet trade, dragged down by earlier losses on Amman's parallel market of newly-listed stocks.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.38 points to 150.12 points in trade worth 490,000 dinars ($692,000).

The Housing Bank, which announced last week it planned to double its capital to 50 million dinars, rose again by 0.05 dinars to 4.77 dinars in trade worth 170,000 dinars, three times the turnover of any other stock.
But its strong performance was offset by a wave of falling shares, which outnumbered gainers by 19 to 12. Shares in another 12 companies were traded but closed unchanged.
Brokers said a sharp fall in the newly listed NAMICO, which produces copper wire for telecommunications and electricity firms, set the tone for a falling market on the main bourse.
"It went down about five percent. It's been hit by waves of speculation -- pessimism and optimism," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investments.
He said investors were divided over whether the company, which has a paid up capital of 30 million dinars, would be able to find a suitable export market for its goods.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.10 percent on Tuesday to 78.84 points, down 5.46 percent since the start of the year.
